question: What is the purpose of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007?
answer: The Act provides for more effective provisions for the maintenance and welfare of parents and senior citizens guaranteed and recognised under the Constitution and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

question: Who is a senior citizen under this Act?
answer: A senior citizen means any person who is a citizen of India and has attained the age of sixty years or above.

answer: Parent means father or mother, whether biological, adoptive or step father or step mother, whether or not the father or mother is a senior citizen.

answer: Maintenance includes provision for food, clothing, residence and medical attendance and treatment.

hi.title: भरण-पोषण का अधिकार
hi.summary: जो वरिष्ठ नागरिक या माता-पिता स्वयं अपना भरण-पोषण नहीं कर सकते, वे अपने बच्चों या पात्र रिश्तेदारों से भरण-पोषण की मांग कर सकते हैं।

question: Who can claim maintenance under this Act?
answer: A senior citizen, including a parent, who is unable to maintain himself from his own earnings or property may seek maintenance from one or more children who are not minors or, in the case of a childless senior citizen, from a relative as provided under the Act.

hi.title: बच्चों एवं रिश्तेदारों का दायित्व
hi.summary: बच्चों और पात्र रिश्तेदारों का दायित्व है कि वे वरिष्ठ नागरिक या माता-पिता का भरण-पोषण करें ताकि वे सामान्य जीवन जी सकें।

question: What is the responsibility of children and relatives under this Act?
answer: Children and, where applicable, relatives having sufficient means are obligated to maintain parents or senior citizens so that they may lead a normal life. A relative is liable where he possesses or would inherit the property of a childless senior citizen, and where multiple relatives are entitled to inherit, the maintenance is payable in proportion to their expected share.

question: Who can file an application for maintenance under this Act?
answer: An application for maintenance may be made by a senior citizen or parent, by any other person or organisation authorised by them if they are incapable, or the Tribunal may take cognizance suo motu.

answer: Yes. During the pendency of maintenance proceedings, the Tribunal may order the children or relative to pay a monthly allowance towards the interim maintenance of the senior citizen or parent.

answer: The Tribunal shall dispose of the application within ninety days from the date of service of notice. In exceptional circumstances, it may extend the period once by a maximum of thirty days after recording reasons in writing.

question: What happens if a maintenance order is not followed?
answer: If the children or relative fail without sufficient cause to comply with the maintenance order, the Tribunal may issue a warrant to recover the amount due and may sentence the defaulter to imprisonment for a term extending to one month or until payment is made, whichever is earlier.

question: Where can maintenance proceedings be filed?
answer: Proceedings may be taken in the district where the senior citizen or parent resides or last resided, or where the children or relative resides. Before hearing the application, the Tribunal may also refer the matter to a Conciliation Officer for an amicable settlement.

question: Who constitutes the Maintenance Tribunal under this Act?
answer: The State Government shall constitute one or more Maintenance Tribunals for each Sub-division by notification. Each Tribunal shall be presided over by an officer not below the rank of a Sub-Divisional Officer of the State.

answer: Any senior citizen, parent, child or relative aggrieved by an order of the Maintenance Tribunal may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of the order. The Appellate Tribunal may condone delay if sufficient cause is shown.

question: What is the maximum monthly maintenance under this Act?

question: When can a property transfer by a senior citizen be declared void?
answer: Where a senior citizen has transferred property subject to the condition that the transferee shall provide basic amenities and physical needs, and the transferee refuses or fails to do so, the transfer shall be deemed to have been made by fraud, coercion or undue influence and may be declared void by the Tribunal.

question: Can a senior citizen enforce maintenance against a transferee of property?
answer: Yes. Where a senior citizen has a right to receive maintenance out of an estate and the estate or part of it is transferred, the right to maintenance may be enforced against the transferee if the transferee had notice of the right or if the transfer was gratuitous.

answer: The State Government may establish and maintain at least one old age home in each district in a phased manner for accommodating indigent senior citizens and prescribe standards for their management.

question: What medical facilities are provided for senior citizens under the Act?
answer: The State Government shall ensure that Government hospitals or hospitals funded by the Government provide beds for senior citizens, separate queues where possible, facilities for treatment of chronic and terminal diseases, and research activities relating to ageing and geriatric care.

answer: The State Government shall give wide publicity to the provisions of the Act through public media, conduct awareness programmes for officers concerned and ensure effective coordination among Government departments dealing with the welfare of senior citizens.

answer: The State Government shall prescribe a comprehensive action plan for providing protection of life and property of senior citizens and ensure its effective implementation through the District Magistrate and other authorities.

answer: Every offence under this Act shall be cognizable and bailable and shall be tried summarily by a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class.

answer: No. Civil courts shall not have jurisdiction in matters that the Maintenance Tribunal or Appellate Tribunal is empowered to determine under this Act, and no injunction shall be granted in respect of actions taken under the Act.
